note: Funding instruments named in the project data. The five funding.source buckets say where money came from in the broadest sense; this table records the instrument that carries the conditions, the co-financing rate and the absorption deadline. A lot is attached to a programme only where its own funding detail names it.

note.en: Bulgaria's share of the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Separate from Romania's PNRR: the two are different national plans under the same Facility, so a figure under one must never be counted under the other.

sources.title: European Commission: Bulgaria's recovery and resilience plan

ebrd-loan.authority: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

sources.title: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development

name.en: Instrument for Structural Policies for Pre-Accession (ISPA)

note.en: Pre-accession instrument, closed on accession. Sections funded through it are the oldest EU-financed works in this dataset.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Instrument for Structural Policies for Pre-Accession

miga-guarantee.authority: Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (World Bank Group)

note.en: A guarantee, not money: it covers a lender or investor against political risk and does not itself pay for works. Counting it as a grant or a loan would double-count the financing it backs.

name.ro: Planul Național de Redresare și Reziliență (PNRR)

ro-pnrr.authority: European Commission / Ministerul Investițiilor și Proiectelor Europene

note.en: Romania's share of the Recovery and Resilience Facility. Milestones have to be met and the money absorbed by the Facility's deadline, which is what makes PNRR-funded openings time-critical in a way ordinary cohesion money is not.

sources.title: European Commission: Romania's recovery and resilience plan
